title: A Single Spin Switches the Steady-State Phase of an Open Quantum System
summary: Changing a many-body system by one constituent is normally expected to produce only a vanishing correction to an intensive observable. Here we show that, above a critical dissipation imbalance, adding or removing one spin at fixed intensive controls switches the steady state of a dissipative collective spin between a phase-averaged ring and a south-polar fixed point. Unlike previous one-spin sensing through dark-state interference, parity here determines whether the Dicke ladder samples an interior zero of the nonlinear jump amplitude.
